blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing international taxes at the intermediate level means keeping track of several jurisdictions at once, each with its own rules, deadlines, languages, and small cultural quirks. A single deal with customers in three countries may involve three different withholding rates, three different documentation requirements, and two overlapping treaties that partially cancel each other out.

The useful habit is to build a small country-by-country profile for each market you sell into. What is the withholding rate? What documents are needed to claim relief? Who is the reliable local advisor? What deadlines exist? Having this in one place, before a deal is signed, turns international tax from a surprise into a checklist.

The advisor we worked with last year said that the secret to good international tax is not knowing every rule, but always knowing whom to ring when you do not. That is exactly the skill the intermediate team is building.

items.q: According to the text, what can a single deal across three countries involve?
options: Three withholding rates and overlapping treaties
A single treaty covering every country
One shared withholding rate for all markets
items.why: "three different withholding rates… and two overlapping treaties that partially cancel each other out."

items.q: What does the text recommend building for each market?
items.why: "build a small country-by-country profile for each market you sell into."

items.q: According to the advisor, the secret to good international tax is…
options: knowing whom to ring when you don't know
items.why: "not knowing every rule, but always knowing whom to ring when you do not."

items.q: The phrase "turns international tax from a surprise into a checklist" suggests the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Tax questions are best handled deal by deal, after signing.
Knowing the deadlines in advance is helpful.
A country profile makes deals more predictable.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende preparar o perfil ANTES da assinatura — lidar só depois de assinar contradiz a tese.

items.q: The mention of "cultural quirks" alongside rules and deadlines suggests that…
options: every country follows the same practices
local context, not only regulation, matters in each market
cultural differences are irrelevant to tax
items.why: Inferência: ao listar peculiaridades culturais junto das regras, o autor indica que o contexto local importa, não só a norma.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando o pacote de perfis de país que está montando. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, this is the tax profile pack I've been putting together for the five markets we're expanding into. The idea is simple: before the commercial team signs anything, they open the folder for that country and they already know what they're dealing with.

Each profile answers four questions. What's the withholding rate? What documents do we need to claim relief under the treaty? Who's the local advisor we actually trust? And what are the deadlines? Nothing clever — just those four, on one page, for every market.

Last week I called the advisor we used in Singapore, and she told me the filing window there was shorter than we'd assumed. If I hadn't rung her, we'd have missed it on the first deal. That's exactly the kind of thing the pack is meant to catch early.

Honestly, I don't expect anyone to memorise the rules. I just want them to know which page to open and which number to call. Prepare before the deal, not after the invoice — that's the whole point.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is James building for the five new markets?
options: A new finance team in each country
A tax profile pack the commercial team can open before signing
A software tool to file taxes automatically
items.why: "this is the tax profile pack I've been putting together for the five markets we're expanding into."

items.q: Which four questions does each profile answer?
items.why: "What's the withholding rate? What documents… Who's the local advisor… what are the deadlines?"

items.q: What did James learn when he called the Singapore advisor?
options: The filing window was shorter than assumed
items.why: "she told me the filing window there was shorter than we'd assumed."

items.q: What does James imply would have happened if he hadn't rung the advisor?
options: The deal would have been cheaper
The team would have missed the deadline on the first deal
The advisor would have called him instead
items.why: Inferência: "If I hadn't rung her, we'd have missed it on the first deal."

items.q: What does James's comment "I don't expect anyone to memorise the rules" reveal about his approach?
options: He values knowing where to look over memorising everything
He thinks the rules don't matter
He wants the team to learn every rule by heart
He plans to remove all the profiles
items.why: Inferência: ele prioriza saber qual página abrir e para quem ligar, não decorar cada regra.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each country is a separate jurisdiction with its own tax rules." A jurisdiction is…
options: a territory where a particular set of laws applies
items.why: Jurisdiction = jurisdição: o território onde vale determinado conjunto de leis.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The two treaties ___, so part of the tax paid abroad can be credited at home."
items.why: To overlap = sobrepor-se; os tratados se sobrepõem em parte.

items.q: "We missed the filing deadline and lost the relief." A deadline is…
options: the final date by which something must be done
items.why: Deadline = prazo: a data-limite para cumprir algo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Before claiming relief, check each country's ___ — some ask for a residency certificate."
items.why: Documentation requirements = exigências documentais, os documentos que cada país pede.

items.q: "The withholding rate in that market is 15%." This is…
options: the percentage of a payment retained as tax at source
the profit margin on the deal
items.why: Withholding rate = alíquota de retenção: o percentual retido como imposto na fonte.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem ao coordenar impostos internacionais. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the tax profile pack." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the country profiles market by market." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "I need to touch base with the local advisor before the deal closes." This means to…
options: make brief contact to check in
items.why: Touch base with = fazer um contato rápido para se atualizar.

items.q: "Legal flagged up a documentation issue in Brazil." To flag up means to…
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo que precisa ser tratado.

items.q: "The team agreed to build the profiles but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry the plan to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
